original_question: Let f(t) be a continuous T-periodic function with f not identically zero and let p>0. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on f that guarantee the singular second-order equation x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t) has positive T-periodic solutions.
target_in_paper: Section 2.6, Problem 9: for the singular T-periodic equation x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t), with f a continuous T-periodic function, f not identically zero, and p > 0, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on f for the existence of positive T-periodic solutions. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s exact target. It has the right equation, the right data on f (continuous and T-periodic, not identically zero), the correct parameter range p > 0, and the correct objective: necessary and sufficient conditions on f for existence of positive T-periodic solutions. This is essentially Problem 9 stated in Section 2.6. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
missing_details: T should be made explicit as a fixed positive period, T > 0, with f: R -> R continuous and T-periodic. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The unknown should be specified as a classical solution x in C^2(R), since the equation involves x''; the paper leaves this implicit in its ODE formulation. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The meaning of 'positive T-periodic solution' should be spelled out as x(t) > 0 for all t and x(t + T) = x(t) for all t in R. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The variable and operator are implicit in the paper and should be made explicit in a stand-alone version: t is the real independent variable and x'' is the second derivative with respect to t. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The nearby context records two necessary conditions that any faithful sharpened version should respect: f must change sign and it must satisfy integral from 0 to T of f(t) dt < 0. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The paper also records the known sharpness landscape around the problem: for p >= 2, those two necessary conditions are sufficient when f has only nondegenerate zeroes; for p = 5/3, they are not sufficient in general, even for smooth f. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))

The quantifiers are for fixed T > 0 and fixed p > 0; the question is to characterize the admissible forcing functions f for that equation, not to broaden the problem to a joint classification in both f and p. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
refined_question: Fix T > 0 and p in (0, infinity). Characterize exactly those nonzero continuous T-periodic functions f: R -> R for which the singular second-order equation x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t) admits a positive T-periodic classical solution x in C^2(R), meaning x(t) > 0 and x(t + T) = x(t) for all t. Any complete characterization should in particular account for the necessary conditions that f changes sign and integral from 0 to T of f(t) dt < 0. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem 9, not a neighboring problem. The introduction explicitly says Section 2 includes a question on a second-order singular differential equation, and Section 2.6 then states Problem 9 almost verbatim in the form your draft is aiming at. The immediate surrounding text supplies the hidden context needed for a stand-alone formulation: the equation is x(t)^p x''(t) = f(t) with T > 0, p > 0, f continuous and T-periodic, and the paper immediately derives the two necessary conditions f changes sign and integral from 0 to T of f(t) dt < 0. It also records the partial positive result for p >= 2 under nondegenerate zeroes of f and the counterexample at p = 5/3, which shows that those two necessary conditions are not sufficient in general. That is why the refined version keeps the scope exactly on characterizing f for fixed T and p, while making the notion of solution fully explicit. ([ddd.uab.cat](https://ddd.uab.cat/pub/artpub/2021/257127/semajou_a2021v78n3p233.pdf))
